memory_update.text: CAMT should remain a high-priority underfollowed AI chokepoint candidate mapped to HBM, chiplet, hybrid-bonding, and advanced-packaging inspection/metrology; next gate is primary-source verification of AI-specific order durability and backlog quality.

COHU should remain a high-priority underfollowed AI test candidate mapped to thermal test, high-socket-force handling, inspection/metrology, interface solutions, and HBM inspection; next gate is evidence of repeat AI/HPC platform adoption across multiple customers.

FORM should remain an underfollowed AI test-hardware candidate mapped to HBM probe cards, logic/foundry probe cards, advanced package test, and possible silicon-photonics test; next gate is evidence that HBM probe demand is supply constrained and structurally durable.

AMKR should be treated as a reference advanced-packaging and OSAT capacity candidate rather than a clean underfollowed small/mid-cap; next gate is durable AI/HPC revenue conversion from high-density fan-out, advanced test, and Arizona capacity.

6239.TW should remain a hypothesis-stage underfollowed OSAT candidate tied to memory backend crowding-out, fan-out panel-level packaging, AI/HPC packaging overflow, and possible CPO exposure; primary-source validation is required.
KLIC should remain a hypothesis-stage advanced-packaging equipment candidate; verify whether HBM-related tools and advanced solutions are material enough to offset legacy wire-bond cyclicality.
AIXA.DE should remain a hypothesis-stage upstream AI photonics equipment candidate mapped to MOCVD/epitaxy for III-V photonics and CPO; verify AI optical-interconnect-specific backlog and lead times.

ALMU should remain a speculative shadow candidate only; evidence must confirm commercial readiness, customer contracts, production qualification, revenue scale, and balance-sheet runway before it can graduate.

OXIG.L should remain a hypothesis-stage photonics process-tool candidate mapped to III-V etch/deposition and CPO manufacturing; verify order intake and backlog specifically tied to datacenter optical interconnect.
The supplied candidate chunk is truncated after Coherent; Coherent and any following candidates should not be fully mapped without the complete Layer 1 candidate records or primary-source evidence.

Need current market capitalization, liquidity, valuation, short interest, analyst coverage, and institutional ownership checks for all names before confirming underfollowed status or market-pricing asymmetry.

Need primary-source filings/transcripts for Powertech, Aixtron, Aeluma, Oxford Instruments, Kulicke & Soffa, and Coherent because the current evidence mostly supports node-level bottlenecks or cached Layer 1 hypotheses rather than company-level AI revenue attribution.

Layer 2C should test falsification signals across the chunk: easing lead times, inventory build, customer insourcing, lower AI/HPC order mix, margin compression, delayed customer qualification, cancelled capex, or evidence that demand is cyclical rather than structurally bottlenecked.

summary: Mapped ticker relationships for the candidate chunk around AI second-order chokepoints: semiconductor inspection/metrology, probe cards, thermal/test handlers, OSAT advanced packaging overflow, bonding/assembly tools, and photonics/CPO upstream equipment. The strongest evidence-backed relationships in this chunk are CAMT, COHU, FORM, and AMKR, where cached Layer 1 evidence directly links the companies to HBM, advanced packaging, AI/HPC test, or OSAT capacity. PTI, KLIC, AIXA.DE, ALMU, and OXIG.L remain hypothesis-stage relationships because the provided evidence supports the node-level bottleneck but not yet enough primary-source company-specific AI revenue attribution. No trading recommendation is made.
